Definition: Percentage of total electricity generation from renewable sources (hydro, solar, wind, geothermal, biomass). Indicates energy sustainability and potential for distributed power solutions relevant to ICT infrastructure in off-grid areas.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score of 0/Unknown was not supported once searched — usable data does exist. World Bank WDI records South Sudan's renewable electricity output at 0.34% of total generation in 2021 (EG.ELC.RNEW.ZS). The I-TRACK Foundation's South Sudan Country Assessment Report (Nov 2025, IEA-sourced) states the country generated approximately 571 GWh of electricity in 2023, of which about 96.3% was thermal (diesel) and around 3.7% solar PV. The cited PMC article confirms continued diesel dominance and limited renewable development. Recalculated to Value Code 1 (<10% renewable share) per the scale.
revised_comments: South Sudan's electricity generation is overwhelmingly diesel-based. IEA-sourced data cited in a 2025 country assessment report put total generation at approximately 571 GWh in 2023, of which around 96.3% came from thermal (diesel) sources and only about 3.7% from solar PV. World Bank data similarly recorded renewable electricity output at 0.34% of the total in 2021. Renewable generation remains well below 10% of total output, reflecting continued reliance on imported diesel fuel and very limited hydro, solar or wind deployment.
